headline: Mayor Olivia Chow and Federal Housing Ministers Announce $140 Million Infill Rental Acceleration
summary: Toronto City Council and federal infrastructure agencies deploy $140 million in housing accelerator funds to fast-track 2,200 non-profit and co-op rental apartments on municipal lands.
body:
TORONTO, ON — Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow joined federal housing representatives to announce a $140 million capital funding agreement under the Housing Accelerator Fund, expediting construction on five municipally owned surplus land parcels.

## Dedicated Non-Profit and Co-Op Rental Housing

The initiative will deliver 2,200 purpose-built rental apartments across Scarborough, Etobicoke, and downtown transit nodes, with 40% permanently designated as deeply affordable units for seniors and working families. Mayor Chow highlighted that leveraging city-owned parking lots and transit hubs cuts development timeline delays by up to 18 months.

Mayor Chow emphasized that building non-profit and public-backed housing is essential to restoring affordability for Toronto workers who are being priced out of the urban core.

## Council Approvals and Development Deadlines

Toronto City Council approved zoning amendments exempting non-profit builders from municipal development charges for projects completed within 24 months.

Non-profit housing federations praised the elimination of municipal development fees.

## Groundbreaking Milestones

Site preparation on the first two residential sites at Victoria Park and Bloor West begins in October 2026.

headline: Mayor Ken Sim Reaffirms 'Zero Means Zero' Property Tax Cap as Vancouver Police Reach Hiring Targets
summary: Vancouver Mayor Ken Sim delivers civic governance address confirming zero municipal tax increases for 2026 while meeting recruiting benchmarks for 100 frontline police officers and mental health nurses.
body:
VANCOUVER, BC — Vancouver Mayor Ken Sim reaffirmed his administration's commitment to the 'Zero Means Zero' municipal tax policy during a civic leadership address, highlighting balanced operational budgets and downtown public safety benchmarks heading into the October municipal election.

## Fiscal Discipline and Police Nurse Deployments

Mayor Sim reported that the Vancouver Police Department (VPD) has successfully filled all 100 new officer positions authorized under council's public safety mandate, paired with Car 87/88 mental health nurse teams. He noted that operational efficiencies and digital modernization within city hall allowed Vancouver to absorb wage pressures without raising municipal residential property taxes in 2026.

Mayor Sim asserted that fiscal discipline and public safety can go hand-in-hand, making Vancouver an attractive destination for tech enterprise and downtown retail revitalization.

## Council Debate and Public Amenities Scrutiny

Opposition councillors argued that freezing property taxes limits funding for community community centre infrastructure in East Vancouver.

Business improvement associations in Gastown and Chinatown reported measurable improvements in foot traffic and street safety.

## Budget Outlook

City staff will present the 2027 preliminary 5-year financial framework to council in November 2026.

headline: Speaker Mike Johnson Promotes Permanent Small Business Expensing Provisions in Federal Tax Package
summary: U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson outlines legislative priorities to make 100% bonus depreciation and Section 199A small business tax deductions permanent in the upcoming fiscal 2027 budget reconciliation.
body:
WASHINGTON, DC — House Speaker Mike Johnson concluded a multi-state congressional economic policy tour, detailing the House Republican legislative agenda to enact permanent small business capital expensing and preserve individual tax reductions ahead of the 2027 statutory expirations.

## Protecting Main Street Capital Investments

Speaker Johnson stated that preserving Section 199A pass-through deductions and immediate equipment write-offs provides stability for manufacturers, agricultural producers, and independent retail businesses facing elevated interest rates. The House Ways and Means Committee has prepared draft statutory language for the upcoming budget reconciliation framework.

Speaker Johnson maintained that pro-growth tax policies empower American job creators and prevent federal revenue burdens from stunting industrial competitiveness.

## Congressional Committee Debate and Revenue Scrutiny

House Democrats argued that permanent corporate provisions expand long-term federal deficits and called for expanding child tax credits for low-income working families.

The National Federation of Independent Business (NFIB) endorsed the permanent expensing framework.

## Legislative Calendar

Floor debate on the comprehensive tax and budget reconciliation act is scheduled following the September congressional recess.

headline: Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries Unveils 'Affordability First' Legislative Framework for Working Families
summary: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries outlines federal legislation to cap grocery supply chain margins, expand Medicare prescription cost limits to commercial plans, and build affordable starter homes.
body:
WASHINGTON, DC — House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries unveiled the 'Affordability First' legislative agenda, outlining Democratic statutory priorities targeting grocery conglomerates, prescription drug manufacturers, and corporate residential landlords.

## Lowering Household Costs and Rent Protections

Leader Jeffries detailed proposed measures to grant the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) direct statutory authority to investigate and penalize algorithmic rent-fixing and corporate price gouging across retail food distributors. The framework also proposes expanding the $35 monthly insulin cap and $2,000 annual out-of-pocket prescription limit to all private employer health insurance plans.

Leader Jeffries asserted that congressional action must focus on kitchen-table economics, protecting middle-class household budgets from uncompetitive market consolidation.

## Partisan Stances and Industry Response

Congressional Republicans warned that price regulations create supply chain shortages and disincentivize private housing construction.

Consumer advocacy groups and labor unions strongly endorsed the affordability package.

## Legislative Strategy

House Democrats will introduce the comprehensive bills as unified discharge petitions during the autumn legislative session.
